pullRequest.title: Add Dockerfile
pullRequest.description: Adds a minimal node:22-alpine Dockerfile so the demo app can run in a container via docker build and docker run.

summary.headline: Adds containerization support with a minimal Node.js Alpine Dockerfile
summary.overview: This PR introduces a Dockerfile that packages the existing tps-demo Express application into a production-oriented container image. The image uses node:22-alpine, installs production dependencies only, copies the application source, exposes port 3000, and starts the server with node index.js. No application code, dependencies, or API behavior are modified.

filesChanged.summary: New multi-stage-style single-stage Dockerfile for running the Express demo app in a container

detailedChanges.description: Uses node:22-alpine as the base image for a small, Node.js 22 LTS runtime
Sets WORKDIR to /app, copies package.json first, and runs npm install --omit=dev to install production dependencies only. This layer-caching pattern speeds up rebuilds when only source changes.
Copies index.js, sets ENV PORT=3000, exposes port 3000, and defines CMD ["node", "index.js"] to start the Express server

behavioralChanges.before: Application could only be run locally via npm install && npm start
behavioralChanges.after: Application can be built and run as a Docker container
behavioralChanges.details: Consumers can run: docker build -t tps-demo . && docker run -p 3000:3000 tps-demo. The container listens on port 3000 by default, matching the app's PORT environment variable default.

behavioralChanges.after: Same application behavior when run inside the container
behavioralChanges.details: No changes to Express routes, middleware, or response formats. The Dockerfile only defines how the existing app is packaged and started.

checks.name: Base image selection
checks.details: node:22-alpine is appropriate for a minimal Express app and aligns with modern Node.js LTS

checks.name: Dependency install strategy
checks.details: package.json is copied before index.js to leverage Docker layer caching; --omit=dev excludes devDependencies

checks.name: Port configuration
checks.details: ENV PORT=3000 and EXPOSE 3000 match the application's default port in index.js

checks.name: Start command
checks.details: CMD uses exec-form ["node", "index.js"], equivalent to npm start without npm overhead

suggestedTests.name: Container health check
suggestedTests.command: docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --name tps-demo-test tps-demo && curl -s http://localhost:3000/health
suggestedTests.expected: Returns JSON with status: healthy and uptime value

suggestedTests.name: Port override
suggestedTests.expected: Server listens on overridden PORT environment variable

items.mitigation: Consider adding a .dockerignore to exclude node_modules, .git, and local artifacts from the build context
For production hardening, consider adding a non-root USER directive

items.risk: No multi-stage build or health check directive
items.mitigation: Acceptable for a demo app; add HEALTHCHECK and multi-stage builds if deploying to orchestrated environments

items.risk: README not updated with Docker instructions
items.mitigation: PR description includes usage; consider adding a Docker section to README.md

recommendations: Add a .dockerignore file to keep the build context small and avoid copying node_modules
Document Docker build and run instructions in README.md
Consider adding a HEALTHCHECK instruction using GET /health for container orchestration
For production deployments, run the container as a non-root user
